NeoSkriptDbEffExecute.name: Execute
description: Runs SQL on a database. The trigger pauses at the line while the statement runs on NeoSkriptDb's own threads, then carries on on its own thread, as after wait.

Each expression in the query's text is sent as a parameter, so a value can't change what the query does. with arguments fills the query's question marks in order, and with batch arguments runs it once for each list in a list of lists.

In a list variable, the rows are stored as {_rows::<column>::<row>}, with each column's name at {_rows::<column>}. In a single variable, the number of rows found or changed, or with generated keys, the key an insert made. If it fails, the variable keeps its value and the last sql error says why.
quickly and synchronously are accepted for older scripts and change nothing.
examples: execute "SELECT * FROM homes WHERE owner = %player's uuid%" in {db} and store the result in {_homes::*}
execute "INSERT INTO scores (name, score) VALUES (?, ?)" in {db} with arguments "Steve" and 100
execute "INSERT INTO homes (owner) VALUES (%player's uuid%)" in {db} and store the generated keys in {_id}

NeoSkriptDbExprDatabase.name: Database
description: A database from its JDBC URL: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL or SQLite. The same URL is the same database everywhere. It connects when the first statement runs, not here.
The lifetime is how long a connection is kept; the driver is a JDBC driver's class.

NeoSkriptDbExprLastError.name: Last SQL Error
description: What went wrong in the trigger's last statement or transaction, or nothing if it worked. A trigger that hasn't run one gets the last error of any.
examples: if the last sql error is set:
send "Couldn't save: %the last sql error%" to console

NeoSkriptDbExprUnsafe.name: Unsafe
description: Puts a text into a statement as it is, rather than as a parameter: for what can't be a parameter, like a table's name. Never use it for anything a player typed.
examples: execute "SELECT COUNT(*) AS total FROM %unsafe {_table}%" in {db} and store the result in {_count::*}

NeoSkriptDbSecTransaction.name: Transaction
description: Runs the statements in the section on that database in one transaction, committed at the end. If one fails, it's all rolled back, the rest of the section is skipped, and the last sql error says why.
examples: execute "UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - 10 WHERE id = 1" in {db}
execute "UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + 10 WHERE id = 2" in {db}

datasource.name: Data Source
description: A database, from the database "...". Shown with passwords as ***. It can be saved in a variable.
